--- apps/desktop/src/main/research/smoke-fixture.ts	
+++ apps/desktop/src/main/research/smoke-fixture.ts	
@@ -0,0 +1,193 @@
+import { readFile, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
+import { join } from "node:path";
+import ExcelJS from "exceljs";
+import { ResearchDataset, type ResearchRecord } from "@reqflow/core";
+import { FEEDBACK_COLUMNS } from "@reqflow/blocks";
+
+export type SmokeAssertion = (condition: unknown, name: string) => asserts condition;
+
+export const SYNTHETIC_FEEDBACK =
+  "Synthetic feedback: <script>synthetic</script><script>window.__reqflowSmokeExecuted = true</script> Seat feels too firm.";
+export const SYNTHETIC_FEEDBACK_ID = "SYNTHETIC-OPINION-001";
+export const SYNTHETIC_MARKER = "Generated smoke fixture. Synthetic only; no BMW or customer data.";
+export const SYNTHETIC_VFC = ["Synthetic seat comfort", "Synthetic seat adjustment"] as const;
+
+/** Generated at runtime only. These two original rows describe one opinion, not two customers. */
+export async function writeSmokeResearchFixture(outDir: string): Promise<string> {
+  const workbook = new ExcelJS.Workbook();
+  workbook.creator = "ReqFlow synthetic smoke fixture";
+  workbook.created = new Date("2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z");
+  const feedback = workbook.addWorksheet("Feedback_Explorer");
+  feedback.addRow(FEEDBACK_COLUMNS.slice(0, 12));
+  for (const vfc of SYNTHETIC_VFC) {
+    feedback.addRow([
+      SYNTHETIC_FEEDBACK_ID,
+      "Synthetic local original",
+      "Synthetic brand",
+      "Synthetic sedan",
+      null, // Unknown market must stay unknown, rather than inheriting the workflow scope.
+      "SYN",
+      "Synthetic propulsion",
+      "Synthetic source-supplied classification",
+      SYNTHETIC_FEEDBACK,
+      vfc,
+      "Synthetic seats",
+      vfc,
+    ]);
+  }
+  workbook.addWorksheet("Smoke metadata").addRows([
+    ["synthetic", "data_origin"],
+    [true, SYNTHETIC_MARKER],
+  ]);
+  const path = join(outDir, "original.synthetic.xlsx");
+  await writeFile(path, new Uint8Array(await workbook.xlsx.writeBuffer()), { mode: 0o600 });
+  return path;
+}
+
+export function verifySmokeResearchDataset(
+  dataset: ResearchDataset,
+  ensure: SmokeAssertion,
+): ResearchRecord {
+  ensure(
+    dataset.sources.length === 1 && dataset.records.length === 2,
+    "one source, two raw records",
+  );
+  ensure(
+    dataset.sources.every(
+      (source) =>
+        source.uri?.startsWith("reqflow-file:///") &&
+        source.reliability === undefined &&
+        source.market === undefined &&
+        source.vehicleLine === undefined,
+    ),
+    "local source identity; no inferred reliability, market or vehicle",
+  );
+  ensure(
+    dataset.records.every(
+      (record) =>
+        record.provider === "local_documents" &&
+        record.originalUrl.startsWith("reqflow-file:///") &&
+        record.collectingAgents.length === 2 &&
+        record.collectingAgents.includes("bmw_sales") &&
+        record.collectingAgents.includes("bmw_strategy") &&
+        record.runIds.length === 1 &&
+        record.runIds[0] === dataset.runId &&
+        record.marketAttribution === undefined &&
+        record.vehicleAttribution === undefined,
+    ),
+    "both collecting agents merged; no inferred record attribution",
+  );
+  const opinions = dataset.records.filter((record) => record.recordType === "feedback");
+  ensure(opinions.length === 1, "repeated feedback rows remain one independent opinion");
+  const opinion = opinions[0]!;
+  ensure(
+    opinion.text === SYNTHETIC_FEEDBACK &&
+      opinion.metadata.feedbackId === SYNTHETIC_FEEDBACK_ID &&
+      opinion.metadata.independentOpinionCount === 1 &&
+      JSON.stringify(opinion.metadata.sourceRows) === "[2,3]" &&
+      JSON.stringify(opinion.table?.headers) === JSON.stringify(FEEDBACK_COLUMNS.slice(0, 12)) &&
+      opinion.table?.rows.length === 2,
+    "verbatim feedback, original ID, 12 columns and both source rows preserved",
+  );
+  const associations = opinion.metadata.sourceAssociations;
+  ensure(
+    Array.isArray(associations) && associations.length === 2,
+    "two original VFC association rows",
+  );
+  ensure(
+    SYNTHETIC_VFC.every((vfc) => (opinion.metadata.vfcAssociations as unknown[])?.includes(vfc)),
+    "both source-supplied VFC values preserved",
+  );
+  ensure(
+    dataset.records.some(
+      (record) =>
+        record.metadata.sheet === "Smoke metadata" &&
+        record.table?.rows[0]?.[0] === true &&
+        record.table.rows[0]?.[1] === SYNTHETIC_MARKER,
+    ),
+    "explicit synthetic metadata preserved",
+  );
+  return opinion;
+}
+
+/** Read real main-process persistence and native-dialog exports, not renderer response fixtures. */
+export async function verifySmokeResearchFiles(
+  outDir: string,
+  dataDir: string,
+  dataset: ResearchDataset,
+  ensure: SmokeAssertion,
+): Promise<string[]> {
+  const exported = ResearchDataset.parse(
+    JSON.parse(await readFile(join(outDir, "research-export.json"), "utf8")),
+  );
+  const saved = ResearchDataset.parse(
+    JSON.parse(await readFile(join(dataDir, `${dataset.runId}.research.json`), "utf8")),
+  );
+  ensure(
+    JSON.stringify(exported) === JSON.stringify(dataset) &&
+      JSON.stringify(saved) === JSON.stringify(dataset),
+    "persisted and exported JSON validate and match renderer IPC dataset",
+  );
+  const workbook = new ExcelJS.Workbook();
+  await workbook.xlsx.readFile(join(outDir, "research-export.xlsx"));
+  const feedback = workbook.getWorksheet("Feedback_Explorer");
+  const records = workbook.getWorksheet("Research Records");
+  const sources = workbook.getWorksheet("Sources");
+  const runs = workbook.getWorksheet("Research Runs");
+  ensure(
+    feedback && records && sources && runs,
+    "XLSX contains feedback, records, sources and runs",
+  );
+  const rowText = (row: ExcelJS.Row, width: number) =>
+    Array.from({ length: width }, (_, index) => row.getCell(index + 1).text);
+  ensure(
+    JSON.stringify(rowText(feedback.getRow(1), FEEDBACK_COLUMNS.length)) ===
+      JSON.stringify(FEEDBACK_COLUMNS),
+    "XLSX feedback headers match export contract",
+  );
+  const opinion = dataset.records.find((record) => record.recordType === "feedback")!;
+  ensure(
+    feedback.rowCount === 3 &&
+      SYNTHETIC_VFC.every(
+        (vfc, index) =>
+          feedback.getCell(index + 2, 1).text === opinion.id &&
+          feedback.getCell(index + 2, 9).text === SYNTHETIC_FEEDBACK &&
+          feedback.getCell(index + 2, 10).text === vfc &&
+          feedback.getCell(index + 2, 25).text === SYNTHETIC_FEEDBACK_ID &&
+          feedback.getCell(index + 2, 26).text === "Feedback_Explorer" &&
+          feedback.getCell(index + 2, 27).text === String(index + 2),
+      ),
+    "XLSX re-expands two associations with matching raw record IDs and original locators",
+  );
+  ensure(
+    records.rowCount === dataset.records.length + 1 &&
+      dataset.records.every(
+        (record, index) =>
+          records.getCell(index + 2, 1).text === record.id &&
+          records.getCell(index + 2, 2).text === record.sourceId &&
+          records.getCell(index + 2, 4).text === record.text,
+      ) &&
+      sources.getCell(2, 1).text === dataset.sources[0]!.id &&
+      sources.getCell(2, 4).text === dataset.sources[0]!.uri &&
+      sources.getCell(2, 9).text === "" &&
+      runs.rowCount === dataset.results.length + 1 &&
+      dataset.results.every(
+        (result, index) =>
+          runs.getCell(index + 2, 1).text === dataset.runId &&
+          runs.getCell(index + 2, 2).text === result.agentId &&
+          runs.getCell(index + 2, 3).text === result.status,
+      ),
+    "XLSX preserves record/source/run IDs, original text, statuses and unknown reliability",
+  );
+  const csv = await new ExcelJS.Workbook().csv.readFile(join(outDir, "research-export.csv"));
+  ensure(
+    csv.rowCount === feedback.rowCount &&
+      Array.from({ length: feedback.rowCount }, (_, index) => index + 1).every(
+        (row) =>
+          JSON.stringify(rowText(csv.getRow(row), FEEDBACK_COLUMNS.length)) ===
+          JSON.stringify(rowText(feedback.getRow(row), FEEDBACK_COLUMNS.length)),
+      ),
+    "CSV matches every XLSX feedback cell, including IDs, verbatim text and VFC associations",
+  );
+  return ["research-export.json", "research-export.xlsx", "research-export.csv"];
+}

--- docs/research/README.md	
+++ docs/research/README.md	
@@ -0,0 +1,390 @@
+# Raw research in ReqFlow
+
+Implementation snapshot: **2026-10-10**. ReqFlow is a **native Electron desktop app**, not a hosted
+research service. Use a Research block to collect provider-returned originals and authorized local
+documents, inspect access/completeness limitations, and export the raw dataset. Collection does not
+create findings, sentiment, reliability scores, priorities, requirements, or human decisions.
+
+The adapters are real implementations, not canned research results. Offline tests inject synthetic
+responses; they do not establish live access or production readiness. See
+[verification](verification.md) for the evidence and the parent-owned final gates.
+
+## Start with a Research-only workflow
+
+1. Open ReqFlow and go to **Settings → AI & research → Web research → Provider**. Select
+   **Firecrawl (recommended)** for original web collection, **Tavily (alternative)** deliberately,
+   or **Off (no web search)** for local-only work. Wait for settings to save before running.
+2. Open **Settings → Research APIs & Zugänge**. Save the selected provider's credential in its
+   masked input, then turn on its **Enabled** switch. Saving a credential does not enable a
+   provider, grant approval, test it, or start collection. Configure other providers separately
+   using the access table below.
+3. Optionally choose **Test connection**. This is an explicit, potentially quota-consuming or
+   paid probe, not a research run. Read the returned capabilities and limitations; a successful
+   probe does not prove source access, platform permission, or complete collection.
+4. Go to **Data Flow** and click or drag **Research** from **Building Blocks** onto the root
+   workplace. For the first run, use only Research blocks: unrelated Raw/AI/HIL/Add to Car
+   implementations and requirement handlers are separate workstreams and may fail with
+   `not_implemented`. No downstream connection is required to collect or export.
+5. Select the block. Set **Research question**, **Market**, **Research agents**, and the result,
+   request, document-page, time, and concurrency limits. Select at least one agent. The current
+   collector uses **Research agents**; the older **Look at** categories do not select agents.
+   Leave **Mastra query planning (paid Anthropic request)** off for deterministic query building.
+6. Optionally enter **Advanced research scope (JSON)** or use **Local original document** to
+   open the native file picker. Keep the Research inner workplace untouched to use the builtin
+   collector. Adding inner blocks or even a boundary-to-boundary edge overrides that builtin.
+7. Click **Run workflow**. The controls save the **whole root graph** and its scope before
+   starting. Expand **Last run** for block states and logs; **Inspect output** shows a preview
+   limited to 20,000 characters, not the complete dataset.
+8. Read the research summary's per-agent states, record/request counts, and limitations. Once the
+   run completes, fails, or is cancelled, choose **Export JSON**, **Export XLSX**, or **Export CSV**
+   and a destination in the native save dialog. Cancelling that dialog writes no export.
+
+**Off blocks both Firecrawl and Tavily**, even with saved keys and enabled switches. YouTube,
+Apify, X, Reddit, OpenAlex, Eurostat, and local documents are independently controlled. There is
+no automatic vendor fallback. An old `anthropic_web_search` setting is readable but unsupported
+for raw originals; explicitly select Firecrawl, Tavily, or Off instead.
+
+For an offline first collection, leave web search Off, leave local documents enabled, select
+`bmw_sales` and/or `bmw_strategy`, and import an authorized synthetic UTF-8 TXT or XLSX. These are
+the two agents with a local-document adapter. Their web branch can be blocked while local originals
+remain available, so read `partial` limitations rather than treating the whole agent as inaccessible.
+The editor and latest-run identity survive tab navigation in the current session; the editor does
+not restore its graph automatically after an app restart. Main persists saved workflows, run
+snapshots, datasets, and outputs; interrupted active runs become failed, not silently restarted.
+
+## Provider access, permission, and cost
+
+Enable only access you are authorized to use. An app switch is not permission from a platform,
+actor publisher, source owner, or data subject. Check current account entitlements, quotas, terms,
+and usage rights before testing or collecting. No fixed subscription prices are promised here.
+
+| Provider        | Credential names                                                   | What you must configure or expect                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
+| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| Firecrawl       | `firecrawl_api_key`                                                | Select Firecrawl in AI & research **and** enable it here. Search discovers URLs; a separate bounded scrape retains returned document markdown, not generated summaries or search snippets.                                                                                                                          |
+| Tavily          | `tavily_api_key`                                                   | Explicit alternative selection and enablement. Only returned raw content/extracts become records; generated answers and snippets do not. Target-access metadata is often unavailable, making useful results partial. Known PDFs are excluded because this adapter cannot enforce a numeric PDF page cap.            |
+| YouTube         | `youtube_api_key`                                                  | Enable Data API access/quota. Collect video descriptions/metadata and available comments/replies. The API-key-only adapter cannot download authorized captions; **transcripts are not guaranteed or collected by this adapter**. Public `textDisplay` may differ from the author's original and is flagged.         |
+| Apify           | `apify_api_token`                                                  | Enable, record granted usage approval, and allow each exact post/comment actor below. Instagram needs supported URLs or literal hashtags, not arbitrary full-text queries. TikTok supports documented search inputs. No downloads, transcription, or paid reply add-ons are enabled.                                |
+| X               | `x_bearer_token`                                                   | Choose `recent` (last seven days) or `full_archive` with the account access required for that endpoint. Historical dates incompatible with recent access block before HTTP. Archive denial never falls back to recent. Queries and minimum-size probes may bill.                                                    |
+| Reddit          | `reddit_client_id`, `reddit_client_secret`, `reddit_refresh_token` | Obtain approval for this intended use, record it explicitly, and configure an identifiable user-agent. OAuth refresh requires `read` or `*` scope. App registration/OAuth consent alone is not research or commercial data-use permission. MoreComments expansion is not implemented; affected threads are partial. |
+| OpenAlex        | `openalex_api_key` (optional in the app contract)                  | Enable separately; actual access/quota depends on the service/account. Records contain reconstructed original abstracts or labeled metadata, **not downloaded full text**. OA PDF links are unretrieved references, not proof that the PDF was read.                                                                |
+| Eurostat        | None                                                               | Enabled by default; select explicit dataset codes and dimension filters in scope. No dataset selection means blocked, not invented statistics. Tables preserve observations/status flags, not conclusions.                                                                                                          |
+| Local documents | None                                                               | Enabled by default; import/select a document in Data Flow. TXT/XLSX are local; complex formats require optional local Docling. There is no automatic cloud parser.                                                                                                                                                  |
+
+Apify's application-owned allowlist contains exactly:
+
+- `apify/instagram-scraper`
+- `apify/instagram-comment-scraper`
+- `clockworks/tiktok-scraper`
+- `clockworks/tiktok-comments-scraper`
+
+Allowing a post actor does not allow its comment actor. A comment-only allowlist cannot enable
+post discovery; a missing comment permission preserves posts with a named partial limitation.
+Actor outputs/builds and account features can change. No arbitrary actor or actor-input override
+is accepted. Returned subtitle links remain links; they are not fetched transcripts.
+
+For Reddit, replace the contact in `desktop:ReqFlow:0.1 (by /u/your_reddit_username)` with your
+approved client's identifiable contact. The Settings input requires 10–200 characters and checks
+the identifiable format. Neither this input nor the approval switch obtains platform approval.
+
+### Credentials stay in the main process
+
+Use the masked Settings inputs, not scope JSON, workflow parameters, prompts, or source URLs.
+**Save** accepts a nonblank draft; **Remove** is the separate deletion action. Drafts clear on
+submission, errors, and leaving the section. Stored values are never returned to credential inputs.
+
+Main encrypts credential values with Electron `safeStorage` and persists only ciphertext in
+`secrets.enc.json`. Reads across IPC return configured booleans/source status, never saved keys.
+Unavailable OS encryption fails explicitly; Linux's `basic_text` backend is rejected instead of
+allowing plaintext fallback. The implemented Research secret store does not read environment keys,
+even though the broader IPC status type/UI can represent `env` for compatibility.
+
+General settings autosave cannot change provider enablement/approval/actor flags: dedicated
+`research.configure` owns them. Credential/configuration changes invalidate old connection reports.
+Connection states are `not_configured`, `untested`, `success`, `invalid_credentials`,
+`permission_required`, `rate_limited`, `unreachable`, and `unsupported`. These are distinct from
+collection outcomes. See [Settings](settings.md) for controller behavior.
+
+Only credentials have this OS-encryption guarantee. Imported originals, datasets, workflow state,
+audit events, and exports are local files, not encrypted evidence stores. Protect their directory
+and exported files with appropriate OS access controls; raw public comments can still contain
+personal information.
+
+## The 13 research agents
+
+The inspector displays IDs with underscores replaced by spaces. Definition labels below come
+from `packages/blocks/src/research/agents.ts`; selection is by the stable shared IDs.
+
+| ID                  | Definition label             | Adapters                               |
+| ------------------- | ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
+| `reddit`            | Reddit discussions           | Reddit                                 |
+| `youtube`           | YouTube videos and comments  | YouTube                                |
+| `instagram`         | Instagram posts and comments | Apify                                  |
+| `tiktok`            | TikTok videos and comments   | Apify                                  |
+| `x`                 | X posts and conversations    | X                                      |
+| `owner_forums`      | Owner forums                 | Selected web provider                  |
+| `editorial_reviews` | Editorial reviews            | Selected web provider                  |
+| `competitor_models` | Competitor models            | Selected web provider                  |
+| `market_studies`    | Market studies               | Selected web provider, OpenAlex        |
+| `regional_context`  | Regional context             | Eurostat, selected web provider        |
+| `technology`        | Technology publications      | Selected web provider, OpenAlex        |
+| `bmw_sales`         | BMW sales publications       | Selected web provider, local documents |
+| `bmw_strategy`      | BMW strategy publications    | Selected web provider, local documents |
+
+All selected agents share one collector request's allowances; duplicate selections run once.
+An agent name is a retrieval focus, not a classification of returned material. For example,
+web documents remain passages unless their source supplies a stronger type. BMW sales/strategy
+web access is narrowed to `bmwgroup.com` and `press.bmwgroup.com` before retrieval.
+
+### Optional native Mastra query planning
+
+The default neutral query builder is deterministic **query construction**, not mock research.
+It still retrieves real originals through the explicitly configured adapters. To opt into paid
+planning, select **Anthropic Claude** in AI & research, set **Fast model** to an Anthropic model ID
+your account actually supports, save an Anthropic key in **API keys**, and turn on the block's
+**Mastra query planning** toggle. Do not assume the preset model strings prove account access.
+
+`mastra.ts` constructs **13 real standalone `@mastra/core` Agent instances** (installed 1.75.0)
+with `{ providerId: "anthropic", modelId, apiKey }`. The key and user-configured model ID are
+injected explicitly; there is no environment-key lookup, model substitution, or fake Mastra model.
+Construction makes no model request. Eligible query-based agents may each make one planning call;
+local reads and explicit Eurostat requests do not need planning. Planning is gated by enabled access,
+credentials, approval, domains, remaining results/requests, and cancellation.
+
+Only bounded search scope/query context goes to the model. **Collected originals, document contents,
+tables, excerpts, source URLs, document IDs, and provider credentials never become planner input.**
+There are no tools, browser, memory, workspace, or analytical outputs. Native structured output
+returns at most three validated queries, with the deterministic neutral query retained. One step,
+768 maximum output tokens, and zero model/processor retries are configured; no extra structuring
+model or repair call is used. Planning failure is visible, not silently replaced with deterministic
+success. Other independent local/non-query collection can still preserve its originals.
+
+## Advanced research scope
+
+Paste a **scope object**, not a `ResearchRequest` or budget object, into **Advanced research scope
+(JSON)**. Unknown keys fail strict validation. The following is configuration only: the official
+BMW URL is an illustrative input, **not a gathered source, a live-access claim, or example evidence**.
+Competitors and dataset filters are operator selections, not findings about these vehicles/markets.
+
+```json
+{
+  "brand": "BMW",
+  "model": "5 Series",
+  "currentGeneration": "G60",
+  "previousGeneration": "G30",
+  "derivative": "Sedan",
+  "propulsion": "BEV",
+  "modelYear": "2026",
+  "markets": ["EU"],
+  "languages": ["en", "de"],
+  "publishedFrom": "2024-01-01",
+  "publishedTo": "2026-10-10",
+  "horizonYears": 5,
+  "questions": ["What experiences are reported about rear-seat comfort?"],
+  "keywords": ["rear-seat comfort", "charging experience"],
+  "competitors": [{ "brand": "Mercedes-Benz", "model": "E-Class", "generation": "W214" }],
+  "allowedDomains": [],
+  "blockedDomains": [],
+  "urls": ["https://www.bmwgroup.com/en.html"],
+  "documentIds": [],
+  "eurostatDatasets": [
+    {
+      "id": "demo_pjan",
+      "filters": { "geo": "DE", "sex": "T", "age": "TOTAL", "time": "2024" }
+    }
+  ]
+}
+```
+
+- Advanced values override the block's question/market/default scope and the automatically computed
+  **Max. age** publication start. Dates are inclusive ISO days; start must not follow end. The
+  example's historical window is incompatible with X recent search: request authorized archive
+  access or choose a compatible window explicitly.
+- `documentIds` accepts imported `file_…` IDs only, not paths or URLs. The native file picker adds
+  its imported ID automatically. **Omit `documentIds` when using that picker**: even an explicit
+  empty array in advanced JSON overrides the picker's selection. For multiple documents, supply
+  the actual IDs returned by `files.import`, never a fabricated ID.
+- Domains are hostname restrictions. Use bare hostnames in examples/configuration. Global blocked
+  domains are unioned with scope blocks; nonempty allowlists intersect. Empty advanced lists cannot
+  clear global restrictions, and a disjoint intersection fails closed. Source hosts, not API endpoint
+  hosts, are checked; an allowlist restricted to BMW will exclude social/OpenAlex/Eurostat sources.
+- Eurostat filters select observation dimensions/periods exactly. The example selects Germany
+  explicitly; `markets: ["EU"]` does not select a Eurostat EU aggregate or rewrite `geo`. A selection
+  is capped at 20,000 observation cells; narrow oversized filters. Publication dates are not
+  observation periods. Language filters are used where each API supports them, not universally.
+- **Requested markets, vehicle identity, query language, author location, and domain names are
+  not customer-country or vehicle metadata.** Missing original Country/Brand/vehicle fields remain
+  blank in feedback views; unknown publication/language/author metadata stays unknown. Never infer
+  customer nationality, ownership, or language from the retrieval scope.
+
+## Bounds, cancellation, and partial results
+
+Set limits before a potentially paid run. The inspector defaults to 10 results, 100 requests,
+20 document pages, 120,000 ms, and concurrency 3. Its result input permits 1–50; the shared
+`ResearchLimits` API permits up to 1,000 results/requests, 500 pages, 900,000 ms, concurrency 8, and
+three GET retries. The block currently forwards the five inspector limits; other shared-limit fields
+(`retries`, `cacheMaxAgeMs`, `maxProviderCredits`, `maxApifyChargeUsd`) are not `scopeJson` settings.
+Shared defaults are two GET retries, cache age zero, no optional credit cap, and $1 per Apify actor run.
+
+- **One Research block invocation = one `ResearchRequest` budget.** All agents/adapters within it
+  share ordinary HTTP attempts (including retries/failures) and planner reservations. Multiple
+  Research blocks in the same workflow receive separate budgets; the merged run dataset is not
+  proof of a workflow-wide spending cap.
+- `maxResults` counts unique normalized raw-record IDs across that request, including passages,
+  metadata, and tables, not just opinions. Duplicate records can add agent attribution without
+  another result slot. Repeated VFC rows are associations with one opinion, not independent results.
+  Agent record counts can overlap; do not sum them as unique opinions.
+- **`maxRequests` is not an absolute physical-network cap.** Up to **four additional, reserved
+  Apify cleanup attempts per HTTP client/request** can abort known actor runs after exhaustion or
+  cancellation. Each uses an independent **five-second deadline**, the same concurrency/endpoint
+  policy, and no retry. This intentional safety overhead is included in reported HTTP/agent counts.
+  It cannot launch actors or abort unknown IDs. Abort does not prove termination or refund charges.
+- HTTP bodies are capped at 16 MiB. Only allowlisted HTTPS provider endpoints are contacted;
+  credentials, custom ports, redirects, and alternate endpoint hosts are rejected. GET alone retries
+  transport/429/5xx failures with bounded backoff; paid POSTs are not blindly replayed.
+- Optional Firecrawl/Tavily credit reservations are conservative, not invoice predictions. They
+  reserve search/extract allowances and Firecrawl's maximum PDF pages before purchase, including
+  failed attempts. Other providers' quotas and billing are separate. Apify's charge setting is
+  **per actor run**, not the sum of discovery plus comment runs. Anthropic input/output tokens can
+  bill separately, including failed/cancelled calls; the query-only contract does not export token
+  usage or monetary totals. **No total physical-cost guarantee is provided.**
+
+Accepted originals survive later provider/schema/page failures, cancellation, or exhaustion and
+are saved cumulatively after each selected agent. Read `success`, `empty`, `partial`,
+`missing_credentials`, `blocked`, `error`, and `cancelled` separately. `empty` means a valid empty
+search, not missing credentials. A wholly unsuccessful empty collection fails the block **after**
+preserving its result details; an absent dataset is an error, not fabricated empty data. A retained
+partial dataset remains exportable. Source-domain filtering and unknown/coarse dates inside a
+requested date window produce explicit limitations, not unqualified completeness.
+
+See [HTTP](http.md), [runtime](runtime.md), and [Apify](apify.md) for accounting and remote-stop limits.
+
+## Local documents and offline availability
+
+Use **Local original document** to import `.txt`, `.xlsx`, `.pdf`, `.docx`, or `.pptx` through the
+native dialog. Main copies the chosen file to the app's local store; source identity is
+`reqflow-file:///<fileId>`, with original artifact IDs/locators, not a private filesystem URL.
+The current Research import does not support `.xls`/`.csv` merely because the separate Raw spec
+lists them. Local reads shared by both BMW agents are cached within a run, not across future runs.
+
+- **TXT/XLSX require no Docling or cloud service.** TXT must be valid UTF-8. XLSX preserves sheets,
+  header/row positions, scalars, nulls, cached formula results, source classifications, units/notes,
+  and cell artifacts. Formulas/macros are not evaluated; links are not followed.
+- Imports/readers cap files at 64 MiB. XLSX adds hard preflight caps: **16 MiB compressed**, **32 MiB
+  expanded ZIP**, **2,048 entries**, **100,000 rows / 512 columns per sheet**, **1,000,000 aggregate
+  `rowCount × columnCount` cells including sparse gaps**, and **16 MiB parsed cell metadata**.
+  Invalid/encrypted/Zip64/oversized archives fail, not silently truncate.
+- Desktop passes the bundled `research-xlsx-worker.js` entry, outside ASAR, to a real Node Worker.
+  It has an empty environment, no inherited `execArgv`, V8 limits of 128 MiB old heap / 16 MiB young
+  heap / 4 MiB stack, a 30-second deadline, and abort termination. These are **not total RSS limits**.
+  A worker failure never falls back to main-thread parsing or cloud. The library's optional
+  in-process compatibility path is not the production untrusted-import path.
+- **PDF/DOCX/PPTX require a separately provisioned local Docling CLI and prefetched models.** Main
+  currently discovers `docling` on its launch `PATH` and requires an absolute
+  `DOCLING_ARTIFACTS_PATH`. There is no GUI executable setting or automatic Python/model installer.
+  A local availability probe can report TXT/XLSX success while complex formats are unsupported;
+  detecting CLI flags does not prove model completeness.
+- The Docling subprocess uses `shell: false`, a restricted environment, offline model flags,
+  disabled remote services/plugins and **disabled OCR**, bounded input/output, page limits where
+  supported, and a 120-second process ceiling (the collection deadline can stop it earlier).
+  Scanned PDFs need a separately approved local OCR integration. DOCX pagination, PDF layout,
+  full document coverage, and transcripts are not guaranteed. No automatic cloud fallback exists.
+
+No real Docling/model-backed conversion was verified on this documentation host, where no `docling`
+command was found on PATH. Use the provisioning/packaging caveats in
+[documents and statistics](documents-statistics.md); verify the chosen runtime offline before
+opening sensitive originals. Native Windows/Linux execution remains untested here.
+
+## Raw identity and export fidelity
+
+JSON is the complete validated raw dataset: `schemaVersion`, `runId`, sources, records, collection
+results, retrieval timestamp, and `synthetic`. Records retain normalized and original source/record
+IDs, original URL/text, provider, collecting agents/run IDs, publication value and
+`datePrecision` (`instant`, `day`, `month`, `year`, `unknown`), language, source-supplied attribution,
+parent/thread/context, locators, tables, metadata, limitations, and content hashes.
+Publication is never replaced by retrieval time. Missing author/user/language values are not
+invented; provider-supplied unknown-language markers remain as supplied.
+
+Normalized URL identity removes fragments/tracking parameters while retaining meaningful query
+parameters. Firecrawl/Tavily copies at the same URL share a publication record; distinct social
+comment IDs are not collapsed just because their text matches. A merge selects the latest
+`retrievedAt` revision and unions attribution/limitations, explicitly flagging changed content.
+Earlier run datasets retain earlier content. This is not an immutable archival guarantee for all
+versions within one run.
+
+### Feedback_Explorer is feedback only
+
+Its first twelve template columns are **ID**, **Source**, **Brand**, **Sales Description**,
+**Country**, **Derivate (e-code)**, **Engine Type**, **Feedback Type**, **Customer Feedback**,
+**Vfc level2 3 Name**, **Vfc level2 Name**, and **Vfc level3 Name**.
+
+Only `recordType: "feedback"` appears in this view/CSV. Studies, product descriptions, forecasts,
+tables, passages, video descriptions, and transcripts do not become customer opinions. Local
+Feedback_Explorer rows with the **same original ID and same text** produce one opinion and multiple
+source-supplied VFC associations. Export expands those associated rows with the **same normalized
+ID**, original feedback ID, sheet, and row. Classification is source-only, not a new AI label;
+different texts under one original ID stay distinct with a conflict limitation.
+
+The supplied Windows reference workbook was unavailable on this macOS host and was **not opened**.
+The reported **4,076 association rows / 2,128 unique feedback IDs** are user-provided reference
+figures, **not verified ingestion counts** or real-data acceptance evidence. The twelve-column
+contract was exercised with synthetic workbooks; no private BMW path/data was inspected.
+
+### Choose an export
+
+- **JSON:** authoritative raw strings/structures. Formula protection and overflow do not alter it.
+- **CSV:** feedback rows only, UTF-8 BOM, quoted/escaped fields, CRLF row separators, and retained
+  embedded newlines. There is no CSV cell-length truncation; use JSON/XLSX for non-feedback records.
+- **XLSX:** `Feedback_Explorer`, `Sources`, `Research Records`, `Metrics Tables`, `Research Runs`,
+  plus `Cell Overflow` when needed. Tables preserve numeric zero, nulls, status flags, dimensions,
+  units, and footnotes instead of interpreting them.
+
+Every XLSX string cell, including serialized metadata and guards, stays within **32,767 UTF-16 code
+units**. Oversized/XML-incompatible values use explicit pointers to bounded ordered overflow
+segments, not unmarked truncation or summaries. Reconstruct by owning sheet/row/column, numeric
+segment order, and parsed **Original Segment JSON**; concatenate, then parse again for structured
+JSON values. Segments do not split surrogate pairs. Standalone CR and CRLF are preserved in the
+written workbook rather than silently normalized by XML.
+
+Spreadsheet strings beginning (after whitespace/control characters) with `=`, `+`, `-`, or `@`
+receive an apostrophe formula guard. **This changes the spreadsheet view**, not raw JSON; cells
+are text, not executable formulas. Do not blindly strip apostrophes to reconstruct originals.
+See [exports](exports.md) for exact reconstruction and lineage rules.
+
+## Developer boundaries and reference
+
+Use the existing typed `api` bridge from renderer code. Do not add renderer `fetch`, filesystem
+access, provider SDKs, or credential reads. The implemented research calls are:
+
+| API                                                       | Arguments / result                                                                                                  |
+| --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| `research.agents()`                                       | Returns all `ResearchAgentDefinition[]`; no collection.                                                             |
+| `research.providers()`                                    | Returns `ResearchProviderStatus[]` with configuration, credential booleans, and connection reports.                 |
+| `research.configure(id, config)`                          | Validated `ResearchProviderId` and complete `ResearchProviderConfig`; persists access flags and returns one status. |
+| `research.test(id)`                                       | Explicit bounded probe; returns one status, does not activate collection.                                           |
+| `research.dataset(runId)`                                 | Returns saved `ResearchDataset`, including partial/unsuccessful results; absent data rejects.                       |
+| `settings.setSecret(name, valueOrNull)`                   | Saves encrypted nonblank credential or deletes on `null`; returns `SecretStatus`, not a key.                        |
+| `files.import()`                                          | Native picker, local copy, `StoredFileInfo` or `null` on cancellation.                                              |
+| `workflows.save(input)` / `runs.start(workflowId)`        | Save validated graph/version, then start the generic engine.                                                        |
+| `runs.blockOutput(runId, blockId)` / `runs.cancel(runId)` | Preserved per-port output / cancellation snapshot.                                                                  |
+| `exports.research({ runId, format })`                     | `json`, `xlsx`, or `csv`; native save dialog, `{ path }` or `null`.                                                 |
+
+Input validation uses shared Zod contracts. IPC errors include `invalid_input`, `invalid_graph`,
+`not_found`, `run_busy`, `invalid_state`, `invalid_file`, `storage_error`,
+`secure_storage_unavailable`, and `secret_storage_error`; arbitrary internal exceptions become a
+fixed `internal` message. Provider/collection reports carry their own access and rate-limit states.
+
+Implementation map:
+
+- Contracts: `packages/core/src/research.ts`, `blocks.ts`, `services.ts`, `ipc.ts`.
+- Native wiring, encrypted credentials, local JSON persistence: `apps/desktop/src/main/research/`.
+- Agent definitions/planning, adapters, normalization, HTTP, exports:
+  `packages/blocks/src/research/`.
+- Shared executor: `packages/engine/src/executor.ts`; renderer controls:
+  `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/dataflow/RunControls.tsx`.
+
+Further reading: [workflow](workflow.md), [runtime](runtime.md), [Mastra](mastra.md),
+[web providers](web-providers.md), [social providers](social-providers.md), [Apify](apify.md),
+[documents/statistics](documents-statistics.md), [HTTP](http.md), [Settings](settings.md),
+[exports](exports.md), and [verification](verification.md). Official provider-documentation links
+and their owners' 2026-10-10 public-document checks are recorded in those subdocs; they are **not live
+API acceptance runs**. No research website fetch is needed to execute the synthetic test strategy.

Pronoun only with one clear referent, else repeat noun. Caveman cut filler; STE keep what make meaning unambiguous. Conflict between them → clarity win.

Tool calls: fire direct. No preamble, plan, or progress note before or between calls. After result: next call direct or final answer never announce next call. Text before call only to clarify, warn security/irreversible, or resolve ambiguity.

Follow explicit reply-language instructions from the user or project. Otherwise preserve the user's dominant language. Never switch because of example text or multilingual context elsewhere. Compress the style, not the language. Every emitted line in that language openings, pre-tool status lines, all not just final reply. ALWAYS keep technical terms, code, API names, CLI commands, commit-type keywords (feat/fix/...), and exact error strings verbatim unless user explicitly ask for translation.

'Drop articles' = article languages only. Where small markers carry case/role (particles, postpositions), keep them grammar, not filler; compress politeness/filler instead.

Answer directly in this style. Skip "caveman mode on", "me caveman think", "Caveman:" prefix or recap redundant with the reply itself. No normal answer plus caveman duplicate. User ask what mode is → say so plainly.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **lite** | No filler/hedging. Keep articles + full sentences. Professional but tight |
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman. No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no long raw error-log dumps unless asked. Standard acronyms OK; no invented abbreviations |
| **ultra** | Strip conjunctions when cause-then-effect stay unambiguous. One word when one word enough. State each fact once. NO prose abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn/auth), NO arrows (X → Y) measured zero token saving under tokenizer, cost decode clarity. Code symbols, function names, API names, error strings: never touch |
| **wenyan-lite** | Semi-classical. Drop filler/hedging but keep grammar structure, classical register |
| **wenyan-full** | Maximum classical terseness. Fully 文言文. 80-90% character reduction chars, not tokens. Classical sentence patterns, verbs precede objects, subjects often omitted, classical particles (之/乃/為/其) |
| **wenyan-ultra** | Extreme abbreviation while keeping classical Chinese feel. Maximum compression, ultra terse |

Example "Why React component re-render?"
- lite: "Your component re-renders because you create a new object reference each render. Wrap it in `useMemo`."
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."
- ultra: "Inline obj prop, new ref, re-render. `useMemo`."
- wenyan-lite: "組件頻重繪，以每繪新生對象參照故。以 useMemo 包之。"
- wenyan-full: "每繪新生對象參照，故重繪；以 useMemo 包之則免。"
- wenyan-ultra: "新參照則重繪。useMemo 包之。"

Example "Explain database connection pooling."
- lite: "Connection pooling reuses open connections instead of creating new ones per request. Avoids repeated handshake overhead."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."
- ultra: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No per-request handshake."

- wenyan-ultra: "池蓄連，免逐請新開，省握手。"

Classical chars = wenyan modes only. Never swap a word to a classical char to shrink at non-wenyan levels.

- Irreversible action confirmations

Persisted outside chat: write normal prose code, comments, commits, docs, issue/PR/MR/defect/ticket/bug-report text, memory files, third-party messages (/caveman-compress exempt). 24:   const errors: string[] = [];
25:   const screens: { name: string; file: string }[] = [];

27:   wc.on("console-message", (event) => {

29:   });

32:   if (wc.isLoading()) await new Promise<void>((r) => wc.once("did-finish-load", () => r()));
33: 
34:   const js = <T>(code: string): Promise<T> => wc.executeJavaScript(code);
35:   const check = (ok: boolean, message: string) => {

37:   };
38:   const go = async (route: string) => {
39:     await js(`location.hash = ${JSON.stringify(`#${route}`)}`);
40:     await delay(500);
41:   };
42:   const count = (selector: string) =>
43:     js<number>(`document.querySelectorAll(${JSON.stringify(selector)}).length`);
44:   const text = (selector: string) =>
45:     js<string>(`document.querySelector(${JSON.stringify(selector)})?.textContent ?? ""`);
46:   /** Clicks the first match; false when nothing matches. */
47:   const click = (selector: string) =>
48:     js<boolean>(
49:       `(() => { const el = document.querySelector(${JSON.stringify(selector)}); if (!el) return false; el.click(); return true; })()`,
50:     );
51:   // Screenshots come from the off-screen renderer's paint events: force a repaint, then wait for it,
52:   // so every screenshot shows the state the checks just verified (capturePage can return stale frames).
53:   let frame: NativeImage | null = null;
54:   let frames = 0;
55:   wc.on("paint", (_event, _dirty, image) => {

58:   });
59:   if (wc.isOffscreen()) wc.setFrameRate(30);
60:   const centre = (selector: string) =>
61:     js<{ x: number; y: number } | null>(
62:       `(() => { const r = document.querySelector(${JSON.stringify(selector)})?.getBoundingClientRect(); return r ? { x: Math.round(r.left + r.width / 2), y: Math.round(r.top + r.height / 2) } : null; })()`,
63:     );

65:   const drag = async (from: string, to: string) => {

1: # Workstreams — how to split the work across agents
2: 
3: Each workstream (WS) owns a set of paths, so parallel agents never edit the same files. Everything
4: builds against the contract in `packages/core` (block specs in `blocks.ts`, graph rules in `graph.ts`)
5: and the block contract in `packages/engine/src/block.ts`. UI workstreams use `@reqflow/core/fixtures`
6: until the API is live. Block workstreams test with fixtures and the `mock` LLM.
7: 
8: ## Starting an agent
9: 
10: Paste [AGENT_PROMPT.md](AGENT_PROMPT.md) into the agent, with the workstream filled in. Agents claim
11: work and hand it off in [STATUS.md](STATUS.md), each editing only its own section. **The concrete,
12: ordered task list for every workstream lives in STATUS.md**; this file defines scope, file ownership
13: and "done when".
14: 
15: ## UI agents (WS2–WS4)
16: 
17: The renderer is sandboxed: no Node, no `fs`, no `fetch` to the internet. Reach data only through
18: `api` from `@/lib/api`. Until WS1 implements a method, it throws `ReqflowError` with code
19: `not_implemented`. Show that state, or render `@reqflow/core/fixtures` meanwhile. Reuse the shared
20: controls in `components/ui/` and the design tokens in `globals.css` (light and dark). Check your
21: screens with `npm run smoke` (screenshots land in `apps/desktop/out/smoke/`), and extend
22: `apps/desktop/src/main/smoke.ts` (ask WS1/WS0) when you add an interaction worth guarding.
23: 
24: ## Git
25: 
26: Use one branch per workstream (`ws1-engine`, `ws2-editor`, …), ideally in its own `git worktree`. Make small
27: commits (`ws<N>: …`), push right away, and rebase on `main` at least hourly. Merge into `main` through a PR
28: with a merge commit, never a squash, so Entire's checkpoint trailers survive. To add a dependency, add it to **your own** package's
29: `package.json` only. If `package-lock.json` conflicts, run `npm install` again.
30: 
31: ## Phases
32: 
33: 0. **Done (lead):** repo skeleton, the contract (`core`: schemas, block specs, graph rules), the block
34:    contract and registry, the default template, fixtures, the app shell with its three tabs, the Data
35:    Flow editor (structure), the Settings page and the Car placeholder.
36: 1. **Parallel:** WS1–WS8 below.
37: 2. **Integration (lead):** wire services and the registry in `apps/desktop/src/main`, run the default template end
38:    to end with `mock`, then with Claude and the real BMW data, then polish the demo.
39: 
40: ---
41: 
42: ### WS0 — Lead / integrator (main session)
43: 
44: **Owns:** `packages/core/**`, `docs/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `PRODUCT.md`, root config files.
45: **Does:** merges branches, reviews and applies contract changes (including block params and ports), runs
46: integration (phase 2) and keeps docs current.
47: 
48: ### WS1 — Engine, persistence & main process
49: 
50: **Owns:** `packages/engine/**`, `packages/db/**`, `apps/desktop/src/main/**`, `apps/desktop/src/preload/**`,
51: `packages/blocks/src/hil/**`, `packages/blocks/src/index.ts`, `packages/blocks/src/templates/**`.
52: **Builds:**
53: 
54: - **First,** the handlers the UIs need: `settings.get/save` (the Settings page already calls them),
55:   `workflows.*` (so the editor can save and load), `files.import` (Raw's file param), and read-only
56:   `requirements.*` / `audit.list` serving the core fixtures until the DB lands.
57: - The executor (see ARCHITECTURE.md → Engine semantics): `validateGraph`, topological run per workplace,
58:   inner workplaces via boundary blocks, merge per input port, per-port output storage, failure →
59:   skipped, pause/resume at HIL, cancel. Wire `BlockContext` (including `ctx.car.add` → DB).
60: - SQLite repositories, versioned requirements, append-only `AuditLogger`, `FileStore`, settings storage.
61: - Every method in `main/handlers.ts` (replace each `notBuilt`), with Zod validation of all arguments. Wire registry, LLM, web search, DB and keychain (`safeStorage`) in `main/`; push run updates via `IPC_EVENTS.runUpdate`.
62: - The HIL block (pause until reviewed, then pass on what the reviewer kept).
63: 
64: **Done when:** executor tests pass with fake blocks (success, failure, multi-port merge, splitter
65: fan-out, inner workplace, pause → resume, cancel). Every IPC method works against SQLite (none left
66: `not_implemented`). A run of fake blocks streams updates to `runs.onUpdate`.
67: 
68: ### WS2 — Data Flow editor UI
69: 
70: **Owns:** `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/pages/DataflowPage.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/dataflow/**`.
71: **State today:** palette, workplace (React Flow), blocks with ports, connect with validation, inspector
72: with parameter forms, inner workplaces with breadcrumb, delete with confirmation, snap/minimap from
73: Settings. The flow lives in memory (`components/dataflow/store.ts`).
74: **Builds next:** save/load (`api.workflows.*`, autosave), "New from template" (`api.templates.list()`),
75: undo/redo, copy/paste, a Run button with live status, counts and logs on each block

77: banner linking to the Car tab.

79: blocks (mocked until WS1 lands).
80: 
81: ### WS3 — Car tab: requirements review & audit UI
82: 
83: **Owns:** `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/pages/CarPage.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/car/**`,
84: `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/requirements/**`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/audit/**`.
85: **Builds:** the Car tab as the output page: the car (keep the car visual) with its requirements as a
86: list or board, grouped by ranking, with filters and sorting. A detail view shows targets, a score
87: breakdown (factor × weight with notes), priority and rationale, an evidence level badge, assumptions,
88: uncertainties and conflicting evidence, and a drill-down from findings to verbatim excerpts to sources.
89: Add a decision bar (approve / reject / defer / challenge) where rationale is required, inline editing
90: with rationale, a History view, a global audit timeline with before → after diffs and filters, a
91: resume-run action, and export.
92: **Done when:** every field from the briefing's deliverable list is visible for the fixture requirements,
93: and the decision and edit flows call `api.requirements.*`.
94:

# Workstreams — how to split the work across agents

Each workstream (WS) owns a set of paths, so parallel agents never edit the same files. Everything
builds against the contract in `packages/core` (block specs in `blocks.ts`, graph rules in `graph.ts`)
and the block contract in `packages/engine/src/block.ts`. UI workstreams use `@reqflow/core/fixtures`
until the API is live. Block workstreams test with fixtures and the `mock` LLM.

## Starting an agent

Paste [AGENT_PROMPT.md](AGENT_PROMPT.md) into the agent, with the workstream filled in. Agents claim
work and hand it off in [STATUS.md](STATUS.md), each editing only its own section. **The concrete,
ordered task list for every workstream lives in STATUS.md**; this file defines scope, file ownership
and "done when".

## UI agents (WS2–WS4)

The renderer is sandboxed: no Node, no `fs`, no `fetch` to the internet. Reach data only through
`api` from `@/lib/api`. Until WS1 implements a method, it throws `ReqflowError` with code
`not_implemented`. Show that state, or render `@reqflow/core/fixtures` meanwhile. Reuse the shared
controls in `components/ui/` and the design tokens in `globals.css` (light and dark). Check your
screens with `npm run smoke` (screenshots land in `apps/desktop/out/smoke/`), and extend
`apps/desktop/src/main/smoke.ts` (ask WS1/WS0) when you add an interaction worth guarding.

## Git

Use one branch per workstream (`ws1-engine`, `ws2-editor`, …), ideally in its own `git worktree`. Make small
commits (`ws<N>: …`), push right away, and rebase on `main` at least hourly. Merge into `main` through a PR
with a merge commit, never a squash, so Entire's checkpoint trailers survive. To add a dependency, add it to **your own** package's
`package.json` only. If `package-lock.json` conflicts, run `npm install` again.

## Phases

0. **Done (lead):** repo skeleton, the contract (`core`: schemas, block specs, graph rules), the block
   contract and registry, the default template, fixtures, the app shell with its three tabs, the Data
   Flow editor (structure), the Settings page and the Car placeholder.
1. **Parallel:** WS1–WS8 below.
2. **Integration (lead):** wire services and the registry in `apps/desktop/src/main`, run the default template end
   to end with `mock`, then with Claude and the real BMW data, then polish the demo.

---

### WS0 — Lead / integrator (main session)

**Owns:** `packages/core/**`, `docs/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `PRODUCT.md`, root config files.
**Does:** merges branches, reviews and applies contract changes (including block params and ports), runs
integration (phase 2) and keeps docs current.

### WS1 — Engine, persistence & main process

**Owns:** `packages/engine/**`, `packages/db/**`, `apps/desktop/src/main/**`, `apps/desktop/src/preload/**`,
`packages/blocks/src/hil/**`, `packages/blocks/src/index.ts`, `packages/blocks/src/templates/**`.
**Builds:**

- **First,** the handlers the UIs need: `settings.get/save` (the Settings page already calls them),
  `workflows.*` (so the editor can save and load), `files.import` (Raw's file param), and read-only
  `requirements.*` / `audit.list` serving the core fixtures until the DB lands.
- The executor (see ARCHITECTURE.md → Engine semantics): `validateGraph`, topological run per workplace,
  inner workplaces via boundary blocks, merge per input port, per-port output storage, failure →
  skipped, pause/resume at HIL, cancel. Wire `BlockContext` (including `ctx.car.add` → DB).
- SQLite repositories, versioned requirements, append-only `AuditLogger`, `FileStore`, settings storage.
- Every method in `main/handlers.ts` (replace each `notBuilt`), with Zod validation of all arguments. Wire registry, LLM, web search, DB and keychain (`safeStorage`) in `main/`; push run updates via `IPC_EVENTS.runUpdate`.
- The HIL block (pause until reviewed, then pass on what the reviewer kept).

**Done when:** executor tests pass with fake blocks (success, failure, multi-port merge, splitter
fan-out, inner workplace, pause → resume, cancel). Every IPC method works against SQLite (none left
`not_implemented`). A run of fake blocks streams updates to `runs.onUpdate`.

### WS2 — Data Flow editor UI

**Owns:** `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/pages/DataflowPage.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/dataflow/**`.
**State today:** palette, workplace (React Flow), blocks with ports, connect with validation, inspector
with parameter forms, inner workplaces with breadcrumb, delete with confirmation, snap/minimap from
Settings. The flow lives in memory (`components/dataflow/store.ts`).
**Builds next:** save/load (`api.workflows.*`, autosave), "New from template" (`api.templates.list()`),
undo/redo, copy/paste, a Run button with live status, counts and logs on each block
(`api.runs.onUpdate()`), an output inspector (`api.runs.blockOutput()`), and a "waiting for review"
banner linking to the Car tab.
**Done when:** you can build the default template by hand, save it, reload it, and see run states on the
blocks (mocked until WS1 lands).

### WS3 — Car tab: requirements review & audit UI

**Owns:** `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/pages/CarPage.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/car/**`,
`apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/requirements/**`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/audit/**`.
**Builds:** the Car tab as the output page: the car (keep the car visual) with its requirements as a
list or board, grouped by ranking, with filters and sorting. A detail view shows targets, a score
breakdown (factor × weight with notes), priority and rationale, an evidence level badge, assumptions,
uncertainties and conflicting evidence, and a drill-down from findings to verbatim excerpts to sources.
Add a decision bar (approve / reject / defer / challenge) where rationale is required, inline editing
with rationale, a History view, a global audit timeline with before → after diffs and filters, a
resume-run action, and export.
**Done when:** every field from the briefing's deliverable list is visible for the fixture requirements,
and the decision and edit flows call `api.requirements.*`.

### WS4 — Settings, app shell & packaging

**Owns:** `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/pages/SettingsPage.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/settings/**`,
`apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/shell/**`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/ui/**` (shared controls),
`apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/lib/settings*.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/lib/theme.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/router.tsx`,
`apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/globals.css`, `apps/desktop/electron-builder.yml`, `apps/desktop/build/**` (app icons).
**State today:** bottom tab bar (⌘/Ctrl 1–3), Settings with App, Global parameters, AI & research,
Collaboration and About; theme switching (system/light/dark); every change validated with the
`Settings` schema. Not saved yet (waits for WS1's `settings.save`).
**Builds next:** API-key entry once `settings.setSecret` exists (never display a stored key), a
`settings.changed` audit entry once WS1 logs it, the app icon and installer config, demo polish.
**Done when:** settings load, validate, save and appear as a `settings.changed` audit event, the shell looks
demo-ready, and `npm run package` produces a working installer on your OS.

### WS5 — Raw block (BMW data ingestion)

**Owns:** `packages/blocks/src/raw/**`, `data/samples/**`.
**Builds:** the Raw block. Params (see `BLOCK_SPECS.raw`): Excel upload (`file` = `{ fileId, name }`
from `api.files.import()`, `sheet`) or database (`dbType`, `connection`, `query`; never store
passwords in params), plus `dataset`. It parses the provided formats (CSV, XLSX and whatever BMW
ships: check `data/raw/` once it arrives) into `Source` + `SourceRecord[]` with locators and language.
Structured datasets (equipment take rates, sales volumes) also emit deterministic `usage_pattern`
findings (for example a high take rate signals a basic expectation) with evidence. Also write
synthetic sample files in `data/samples/` that match the real formats. Param changes → request via WS0.
**Done when:** each sample dataset ingests in tests, errors name the bad row or column, and no data is dropped silently.

### WS6 — Research block

**Owns:** `packages/blocks/src/research/**`.
**Builds:** the Research block. It turns its params and the scope into queries (competitors in the
segment, owner and press reviews, market and technology trends for the horizon), runs them through
`ctx.web`, fetches pages and extracts clean text into `SourceRecord`s — the same stream format as Raw —
and sets the `Source` kind, publisher, date and **reliability** (with the rule documented). It respects
allowed and blocked domains and de-duplicates by URL. Also implement `WebSearch` providers
(`anthropic_web_search`, `tavily`) as factories that take keys as arguments (WS1 wires them).
**Done when:** a recorded or offline test run produces sources with working URLs and reliability, and failures are logged rather than swallowed.

### WS7 — AI blocks: AI Filter, AI Splitter, Add to Car

**Owns:** `packages/llm/**`, `packages/blocks/src/ai-filter/**`, `packages/blocks/src/ai-splitter/**`,
`packages/blocks/src/add-to-car/**`.
**Builds:** an `LlmClient` with a Claude provider and a deterministic `mock` provider (use the `claude-api`
skill for SDK details). **AI Filter**: keep items matching the criterion and extract evidence-linked
findings (verbatim-excerpt verification; out-of-scope items logged with a reason). **AI Splitter**:
route every item to exactly one branch (`out-<i>`); "Split by: Priority" uses WS8's scoring.
**Add to Car**: cluster and derive customer-facing, actionable requirements (IDs from
`formatRequirementId`, measurable targets, evidence level per the A–D rule, Kano class, assumptions,
uncertainties, conflicting findings), set the priority from the input port's ranking, and hand them
to `ctx.car.add`. Also export `answerChallenge(...)` for the API's challenge flow.
**Done when:** fixture records → filter → splitter → Add to Car runs fully offline with `mock`, all
outputs parse against the core schemas, and every finding's excerpt is verified.

### WS8 — Prioritization

**Owns:** `packages/blocks/src/prioritization/**`.
**Builds:** explainable scoring used by the AI Splitter's priority mode. Factors are computed
deterministically where possible: customer impact from mentions, sentiment and sales volume; evidence
strength from independent sources × reliability and evidence level; competitive gap from
`competitor_advantage` findings; trend momentum from `market_trend` findings. The LLM is used only
where a judgement is needed (brand fit, ease), always with a one-line note. It uses `weightedTotal`
and `priorityForScore` and writes a readable `priorityRationale` naming the top drivers. It also flags
"high score, weak evidence".
**Done when:** scores are reproducible for the fixtures, changing Settings weights changes the ranking as
expected (tested), and each factor has a note a PM can understand.

61: function publicHost(url: URL): string {
62:   const host = url.hostname.toLowerCase().replace(/\.$/, "");
63:   if (
64:     !/^https?:$/.test(url.protocol) ||
65:     url.username ||
66:     url.password ||
67:     url.port ||
68:     isIP(host.replace(/^\[|\]$/g, "")) ||
69:     !host.includes(".") ||
70:     /(?:^|\.)(?:localhost|local|internal|lan|home|localdomain|test|invalid|example|onion)$/.test(
71:       host,
72:     ) ||
73:     !host.split(".").every((label) => /^[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?$/.test(label))
74:   )
75:     throw new Error(
76:       "Research source must have a public HTTP(S) hostname without credentials or custom ports.",
77:     );
78:   return host;
79: }

81: /** Normalize domain policy once, so every provider receives the same hostname semantics. */
82: function domains(values: string[]): string[] {
83:   return [
84:     ...new Set(
85:       values.map((value) => {
86:         const trimmed = value.trim().replace(/^(https?:\/\/)?\*\./i, "$1");
87:         if (!trimmed || /\s/.test(trimmed))
88:           throw new Error("Research domain filters must contain valid hostnames or HTTP(S) URLs.");
89:         return publicHost(new URL(/^https?:\/\//i.test(trimmed) ? trimmed : `https://${trimmed}`));
90:       }),
91:     ),
92:   ];
93: }

95: const matchesHost = (host: string, domain: string) =>
96:   host === domain || host.endsWith(`.${domain}`);
97: function intersectDomains(left: string[], right: string[]): string[] {
98:   return [
99:     ...new Set(
100:       left.flatMap((a) =>
101:         right.flatMap((b) => (matchesHost(a, b) ? [a] : matchesHost(b, a) ? [b] : [])),
102:       ),
103:     ),
104:   ];
105: }

107: /** A scoped allowlist may narrow global access; an empty intersection never means unrestricted. */
108: export function mergeResearchDomainPolicy(
109:   global: Pick<ResearchScope, "allowedDomains" | "blockedDomains">,
110:   scoped: Pick<ResearchScope, "allowedDomains" | "blockedDomains">,
111: ): Pick<ResearchScope, "allowedDomains" | "blockedDomains"> {
112:   const globalAllowed = domains(global.allowedDomains);
113:   const scopedAllowed = domains(scoped.allowedDomains);
114:   const allowedDomains =

123:     );

125:     allowedDomains,
126:     blockedDomains: [

132: function sourceDomains(agent: ResearchAgentId, provider: ResearchProviderId): string[] {

327:     const headers = Array.from({ length: width }, (_, i) => {
328:       const value = scalar(headerCells.get(i + 1)?.value ?? null);
329:       return value === null ? "" : String(value);
330:     });
331:     const rows: CellValue[][] = [],
332:       sourceRows: number[] = [],
333:       footnotes: string[] = [];
334:     const cellArtifacts: { address: string; value: unknown; note?: unknown; numFmt?: string }[] =
335:       [];
336:     for (let row = headerRow || 1; row <= sheet.rowCount; row++) {
337:       if (row % 128 === 0) {
338:         await setImmediate();
339:         cancelled(signal);
340:       }
341:       const values = Array<CellValue>(width).fill(null);
342:       for (const cell of existingRows.get(row) ?? []) {
343:         const note = noteText(cell.note);
344:         if (note) footnotes.push(note);
345:         if (
346:           (cell.value && typeof cell.value === "object") ||
347:           cell.note ||
348:           (cell.numFmt && cell.numFmt !== "General")
349:         ) {
350:           cellArtifacts.push({
351:             address: cell.address,
352:             value: cell.value,
353:             note: cell.note,
354:             numFmt: cell.numFmt,
355:           });
356:         }
357:         values[cell.column - 1] = scalar(cell.value);
358:       }
359:       if (row > headerRow) {
360:         rows.push(values);
361:         sourceRows.push(row);
362:       }
363:     }
364:     const table = {
365:       headers,
366:       rows,
367:       units: units(headers, rows),
368:       footnotes,
369:       dimensions: { sheet: sheet.name, headerRow, sourceRows },
370:     };
371:     const special =
372:       normalized(sheet.name) === "feedbackexplorer" ||
373:       (workbook.sheets.length === 1 &&
374:         normalized(path.parse(fileName).name) === "feedbackexplorer");
375:     if (!special) {
376:       items.push(
377:         CollectedItem.parse({
378:           ...base(fileId),
379:           recordId: `${fileId}:sheet:${sheet.id}`,
380:           recordType: "table",
381:           text: textTable(table),
382:           locator: `${sheet.name}!rows ${headerRow}-${sheet.rowCount}`,
383:           table,
384:           metadata: {
385:             ...artifact(fileId),
386:             sheet: sheet.name,
387:             sheetId: sheet.id,
388:             headerRow,
389:             sourceRows,
390:             cellArtifacts,
391:           },
392:           limitations: [
393:             "XLSX first nonempty row is preserved as header; no semantic classification inferred. Formulas use saved results only, never evaluated. maxPages does not truncate spreadsheet sheets.",
394:           ],
395:         }),
396:       );
397:       continue;
398:     }
399:     const idColumn = column(headers, ["id", "feedbackid", "commentid", "responseid"]);
400:     const textColumn = column(headers, [
401:       "text",
402:       "feedback",
403:       "feedbacktext",
404:       "customerfeedback",
405:       "verbatim",
406:       "comment",
407:       "commenttext",
408:     ]);
409:     const vfcColumns = headers
410:       .map((header, i) => (normalized(header).startsWith("vfc") ? i : -1))
411:       .filter((i) => i >= 0);
412:     if (idColumn < 0 || textColumn < 0 || !vfcColumns.length)
413:       throw new ProviderError(
414:         "unsupported",
415:         "Feedback_Explorer requires explicit ID, text and VFC headers.",
416:       );
417:     const classificationColumns = headers
418:       .map((header, i) =>
419:         /^(sentiment|classification|category|topic|kano|feedbacktype)/.test(normalized(header))
420:           ? i
421:           : -1,
422:       )
423:       .filter((i) => i >= 0);
424:     const artifactsByRow = new Map<number, typeof cellArtifacts>();
425:     for (const cell of cellArtifacts) {
426:       const number = Number(cell.address.replace(/^[A-Z]+/, ""));
427:       const existing = artifactsByRow.get(number) ?? [];
428:       existing.push(cell);
429:       artifactsByRow.set(number, existing);
430:     }
431:     const marketColumn = column(headers, ["market", "country", "geography"]),
432:       vehicleColumn = column(headers, ["vehicle", "model", "vehicleline"]);
433:     for (const [index, row] of rows.entries()) {
434:       if (index % 128 === 0) {
435:         await setImmediate();
436:         cancelled(signal);
437:       }
438:       if (row.every((value) => value === null)) continue;
439:       const id = row[idColumn],
440:         text = row[textColumn],
441:         rowNumber = sourceRows[index]!;
442:       if (id === null || id === undefined || typeof text !== "string" || !text.length)
443:         throw new ProviderError(
444:           "unsupported",
445:           "Feedback_Explorer row requires ID and source text.",
446:         );

448:       let entry = feedback.get(key);
449:       const texts = idTexts.get(String(id)) ?? new Set<string>();
450:       texts.add(text);
451:       idTexts.set(String(id), texts);
452:       if (!entry) {
453:         const explicit = (i: number) =>
454:           i >= 0 && row[i] !== null && row[i] !== undefined
455:             ? {
456:                 value: String(row[i]),
457:                 origin: "source_explicit",
458:                 locator: `${sheet.name}!${cellAddress(i + 1, rowNumber)}`,
459:               }
460:             : undefined;
461:         entry = {
462:           rows: [],
463:           sourceRows: [],
464:           vfc: [],
465:           classifications: [],
466:           item: CollectedItem.parse({
467:             ...base(fileId),
468:             sourceKind: "customer_feedback",
469:             recordId: `${fileId}:feedback:${createHash("sha256").update(key).digest("hex").slice(0, 24)}`,
470:             recordType: "feedback",
471:             text,
472:             locator: `${sheet.name}!row ${rowNumber}`,
473:             market: explicit(marketColumn),
474:             vehicle: explicit(vehicleColumn),
475:             metadata: {
476:               ...artifact(fileId),
477:               feedbackId: String(id),
478:               sheet: sheet.name,
479:               independentOpinionCount: 1,
480:               cellArtifacts: artifactsByRow.get(headerRow) ?? [],
481:               sourceAssociations: [],
482:             },
483:             table: {
484:               headers,
485:               rows: [],
486:               units: units(headers, [row]),
487:               footnotes: [],
488:               dimensions: { sheet: sheet.name, headerRow, sourceRows: [] },
489:             },
490:             limitations: [
491:               "Feedback classifications and VFC associations are source-supplied, not independent opinions or model inferences.",
492:             ],
493:           }),
494:         };
495:         feedback.set(key, entry);
496:       }
497:       const associations = entry.item.metadata.sourceAssociations as unknown[];
498:       associations.push({ sheet: sheet.name, row: rowNumber, headers, values: row });
499:       const rowArtifacts = artifactsByRow.get(rowNumber) ?? [];
500:       (entry.item.metadata.cellArtifacts as unknown[]).push(
501:         ...rowArtifacts.map((cell) => ({ sheet: sheet.name, ...cell })),
502:       );
503:       if (entry.item.table) {
504:         for (const cell of rowArtifacts) {
505:           const note = noteText(cell.note as ExcelJS.Comment | string | undefined);
506:           if (note) entry.item.table.footnotes.push(note);
507:         }
508:       }
509:       for (const [attribute, i] of [
510:         ["market", marketColumn],
511:         ["vehicle", vehicleColumn],
512:       ] as const) {
513:         if (
514:           entry.item[attribute] &&
515:           i >= 0 &&
516:           row[i] !== null &&
517:           row[i] !== undefined &&
518:           entry.item[attribute]?.value !== String(row[i])
519:         ) {
520:           entry.item[attribute] = undefined;
521:           entry.item.limitations.push(
522:             `Conflicting source-explicit ${attribute} values across feedback associations; no single attribution retained.`,
523:           );
524:         }
525:       }
526:       if (
527:         entry.item.table &&
528:         JSON.stringify(entry.item.table.headers) !== JSON.stringify(headers)
529:       ) {
530:         // Preserve heterogeneous associations as original structured rows, never under wrong headers.
531:         entry.item.table = undefined;
532:         entry.item.limitations.push(
533:           "Feedback associations span different sheet headers; consult sourceAssociations for original rows.",
534:         );
535:       }
536:       entry.rows.push(row);
537:       entry.sourceRows.push(rowNumber);
538:       for (const i of vfcColumns)
539:         if (row[i] !== null && row[i] !== undefined && !entry.vfc.includes(String(row[i])))
540:           entry.vfc.push(String(row[i]));
541:       for (const i of classificationColumns)
542:         if (row[i] !== null && row[i] !== undefined)
543:           entry.classifications.push({
544:             column: headers[i]!,
545:             value: row[i]!,
546:             origin: "source_explicit",
547:             locator: `${sheet.name}!${cellAddress(i + 1, rowNumber)}`,
548:           });
549:     }
550:   }
551:   for (const entry of feedback.values()) {
552:     if ((idTexts.get(String(entry.item.metadata.feedbackId))?.size ?? 0) > 1)
553:       entry.item.limitations.push(
554:         "Same feedback ID has different texts; conflicting source texts are kept separately.",
555:       );
556:     entry.item.metadata.sourceRows = entry.sourceRows;
557:     entry.item.metadata.vfcAssociations = entry.vfc;
558:     entry.item.metadata.classifications = entry.classifications;
559:     if (entry.item.table) {
560:       entry.item.table.rows = entry.rows;
561:       entry.item.table.dimensions = {
562:         sheet: entry.item.metadata.sheet,
563:         sourceRows: entry.sourceRows,
564:       };
565:     }
566:     items.push(CollectedItem.parse(entry.item));
567:   }
568:   return items;
569: }
